I really love this app; I'm a studen in University and I can now be taken back to a class I was studying for by hearing one of these soundscapes, which is a really interesting experience to say the least. What I really use Portal for, however, is to sleep. 
After listening to a podcast about the Amazon rainforest, I now go to sleep listening to "Twilight rainforest" in St. Lucia. 
When I read fiction, I always put on that "Spring Barley Field" and it takes me straight into fairytale land. 
When I want white noise like sound for sleep or focus, why not do it in beautiful "Ama Dablam" in Nepal, or my all time favorite "Highlands Snow" in Scotland (seriously this one is just perfect).
I've woken up to "Fingle Woods" birds chirping so much that I once was kind of confused where I was when I woke up.
And then, there's Stuart Chan at Portal, who's the goat. They hooked me up with the beta for Mac so I could try it early and "help out" by using it and find bugs (little do they know they were the ones helping me hehe). Speaking of, any bugs I did find Stuart instantly responded to and it was fixed so quickly.

Yes, it's expensive, and I'll be sad when my year subscription ends come november - because I'm in my final year of university and I need all the spare change I can get. But as soon as I'm able, I plan on putting my money where my mouth is, and I suggest you do too (on your mouth that is, I don't want your money on my mouth).

Here's to portals to better worlds; or has it been our beautiful world all along?
Love it, peaceful serene.

I didn't think the desktop version of Portal could be that much better than any other "background noise" app—I was wrong. The whole experience is so seamless and so gorgeous that it blows any other app I've tried out of the water. Having these vistas as the *true* background to daily computer activities feels so indulgent and peaceful. 

You definitely want to try this.

This app saved me last semester and I'm sure it will have the same effect this semester. It dramatically improved my ability to not only focus when I needed to focus, but relax and calm down when the stresses of school got to be too much to handle. 10/10

title.label: The best work-from-home tool I've found

content.label:
Portal is that rare app that's worthy of your time and attention because that's precicely what it gives you in return—time and attention. It's. so. zen.

I've used Portal on my iPhone for a couple of years, projecting it to my Homepod for pleasant morning birdsong and water lapping on the shores of Lake Bled, or Triglav thunderstorms for a soothing night's sleep; I've even taken the birds of Fingle Woods with me on my walks while I simultaneously listen to a podcast or audiobook.

But the desktop app brings a whole new dimension to the experience. I'm mesmerized by the beauty of the video taking over my desktop background in its gentle, near-seamless loop. It's a window into the outside world—any outside world that you want right now. Is it a river? A waterfall? A beach? A field? A rainy forest? Portal has brought my mind to a whole new place of focus and productivity I hadn't felt for some time. I adore it. This is a uniquely poignant and important productivity tool, the true missing piece in the remote worker's arsenal. You might try mixing it with music, too—I always love a good afternoon Lo-Fi listen—and see where your focus takes you.

I've been in contact with the team behind Portal, and they're a pleasure to talk with. They take feedback sincerely and their craft seriously. I can't wait to see what they bring to Portal next!

title.label: A Gateway to Immersive Escapes: Portal App Review

content.label:
I recently discovered the macOS app Portal - Immersive Escapes, and I can confidently say that it has transformed my desktop experience in the most captivating way possible. This app has completely redefined the concept of desktop wallpapers, taking them from static images to breathtaking live views of awe-inspiring locations. It's an absolute gem!

First and foremost, the level of immersion that Portal provides is unparalleled. Every time I glance at my desktop, I'm instantly transported to a different place. Whether it's the serene beauty of a tropical beach, the majestic grandeur of a mountain range, or the vibrant energy of a bustling cityscape, I'm treated to a dynamic visual feast that never fails to captivate me.

What sets Portal apart is the attention to detail. The developers have not only provided stunning visuals but have also incorporated ambient sounds that match each location. The gentle waves crashing on the shore, the chirping of birds in a lush forest, or the distant sounds of a bustling market—it's the perfect symphony that complements the visual experience and makes it feel incredibly realistic.

The app itself is user-friendly and intuitive. It seamlessly integrates into macOS, allowing for easy customization and navigation. Setting up a new location as my wallpaper is as simple as a few clicks, and the app provides a vast collection of high-quality locations to choose from. Additionally, the option to schedule wallpaper changes based on the time of day or specific intervals adds an extra touch of variety to keep things fresh.

One aspect that pleasantly surprised me was the app's performance. Despite the dynamic nature of the live wallpapers, Portal has been incredibly efficient in terms of system resource usage. It runs smoothly in the background without affecting the overall performance of my Mac. This attention to optimization is commendable and greatly appreciated.

The developers behind Portal have consistently provided updates and new content, ensuring that the app remains fresh and exciting. They genuinely listen to user feedback and incorporate suggestions, making it clear that they are dedicated to delivering an exceptional experience to their users.

In conclusion, Portal - Immersive Escapes is a game-changer in the world of desktop customization. It goes above and beyond traditional wallpapers, transforming your workspace into a gateway to mesmerizing locations. With its stunning visuals, immersive sounds, user-friendly interface, and outstanding performance, this app has won my heart. I wholeheartedly recommend Portal to anyone seeking a truly captivating and immersive desktop experience.

Disclaimer: This review is based on my personal experience with the app and is in no way influenced or sponsored.

I started with the iOS app in it's infancy, then started using it on my iPad, then when I heard about the MacOS beta, I practically begged to be a part of it.

I've enjoyed each iteration and have seen consistent improvement along the way.  The looping got better, the presentation quality more consistent.

I have very few criticims of the app, and even fewer of the team.  I've engaged with them a few times, and found them to be incredibly responsive and downright pleasant to deal with.

I don't know that my productivity has improved drastically, or if at all, but I will say that this app adds color and depth to my work day, as I spend most of it in my office on my laptop, working with data and code.  To have my Mac running Portal as I work, lookng through a window into a paradise far from my office, and to hear the vibrant sounds that accompany the sight improves my state of mind.

title.label: An Experience in Beauty and Excellenc

content.label: This is one of the best thought out and executed experiences in any app I've encountered. With it on my iPhone, iPad, and now iMac, I delight in the beauty of these scenes and the ambient sound to accompany them. And it's all done at the highest quality possible with no shortcuts. It's been a joy to experience while working, reading, and sleeping. I don't throw the word around - this is excellence.
Reduced my anxiety greatly and increased my productivity.

Full disclosure...I've been using the iOS version of this since it came out. The background screen is totally awesome, especially when you add in the water animation. I find this really relaxing. One thing I do miss from the iOS version, though, are the timers. When you selected a Mode (Focus, etc.) you could also set a timer so it would "bring you back to reality" as it were. I always found this really useful and miss it here. Of course being able to download portals like you can in the iOS version would be nice as well, but that's in no way a deal-breaker. This is one of the best ambient sound apps I've ever seen, and the looping sound isn't really noticable (unlike some others outt here).

A true successor to Naturespace, my most used iOS app of all time (dont even wanna know the amount of waking hours I spent with it, not to mention sleeping). That’s pretty much the highest praise I can give. 

The Spatial Audio is awesome too….it gives everything a less dense and airier, more diffuse sound that feels more like a huge, dynamic open space.   

Outside of the scope of this app, but I would love these guys to do the usual house sounds like air conditioner, ceiling fan, washer/dryer, etc

title.label: Been waiting for the Mac app for years. Blown away!

content.label: I've been using Portal on iPad (for focus and meditation) and iPhone (for sleep) since right after their launch. Every few months I check if there is a Mac app so I don't always have to keep my iPad nearby to use it. I finally saw the Mac app last week and WOW was I blown away. They've really taken the app to the next level rather than just going with a more simple port. The dynamic desktop and degree of immersion are incredible, especially on large displays. The ease of access in the menu bar is great too, as are so many other little details. Couldn't recommend it more highly!

This app is phenomenal. The total immersion creates such a relaxing atmostphere while you work on the computer. Polished sounds and graphics really highlight the apple experience. Get it! You won't regret it.

title.label: Works well, but I think it's overpriced

content.label: It's a well done and well integrated app.  I think compared to its competitors, even considering its features, I think the IAP is too high.  $20-30/yr. would have been more amenable.

title.label: This is the Pinnacle of Focus Music

content.label:
As someone who has listened to hundreds of hours of nature sounds on YouTube and Spotify, I can't describe how much it annoys me when the sound isn't quite perfect. A stream is too loud, or you realize the birds are just on loop. Sometimes the rain noises stutter and it completely breaks your flow.
Portal is different. I don't know how they do it: anything you listen to on here is guaranteed to be crisp, non-looped and immersive.

This is a phenomenal app.  I love the beautiful scenery from all over the world.  It's worth the price and I look forward to additional downloads in the future.  I love the Focus, Create, and Escape themes!  Also, the Featured Collections is a great way to experience additional landscapes.

A couple enhancements that I would propose:
- create a screensaver option for the selected imagery. 
- create an option to cycle through Features Collections based on timed increments or new logins (like other Desktop picture) features.
- fix the memory leak, as Portal crashes about once a day when left running.

I can't wait to see what you do next.  It's one of the best apps in the AppStore.
